newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London held steady throughout a slow trading day and at the close the March contract was unchanged at $303.70 per tonne while May was up $0.10 at $304.30 per tonne. The two-day Thanksgiving holiday closure of the New York raw sugar market was blamed for the lack of action which is expected to continue through tomorrow, traders said.

RUSSIA - Russia's 1996 sugar beet output has been revised up to 15.1 million tonnes from 14.9 million tonnes, according to the State Statistics Committee figures released recently covering output on all farms. Government forecasts earlier this year had targeted a 1996 harvest of 16.0 million tonnes. Around 4 per cent of the beet harvest is grown on private farms.

GUATEMALA - Guatemala will produce a record sugar crop of 1.36 million tonnes, tel quel, in 1996/97 (November/June), up from 1.28 million tonnes produced in the like period the previous year. According to the Sugar Growers Association of Guatemala, predictions for a larger harvest were based on an additional 5,000 to 8,000 ha under cane this year as well as hopes for better yields. 15 of the country's 17 sugar mills are already operating and it is expected that all will be up and running soon and throughout most of the harvest. Sugar growers anticipate they will export approximately 70 per cent of the crop. Cane yields this year were slightly up on last year's 93 tonnes per ha while sugar content is approximately 10.3 per cent which is at the high end of last year's range. Principal destinations for Guatemalan sugar are the United States, Peru, Russia and Venezuela.

BRAZIL - Brazil total sugar output for the 1996/97 (May/April) crop year hit 11.2 million tonnes, tel quel, as of November 16, the Industry and Commerce Ministry recently said. Production in the corresponding period the previous year was 10.3 million tonnes. In the center-south a total of 9.8 million tonnes was produced compared to 8.8 million tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Brazil's government plan for the 1996/97 crop year made provisions for a center-south sugar production of 10.47 million tonnes. According to the Association of the Sugar and Alcohol Industry of Sao-Paulo (AIAA) center-south producers so far milled 217 million tonnes of sugar cane compared to 189 million tonnes the previous year and produced a total of 11.4 billion litres of alcohol against 10.1 billion litres in 1995/96. According to industry sources, harvesting will continue through the end of December, slightly later than usual due to rain related harvesting delays which occurred in mid November.

USDA - According to the US Department of Agriculture, sugar production in 1996/97 will reach a record 125 million tonnes, up 2 per cent from last year's output. World sugar trade will rise by 1 per cent to 35.5 million tonnes from 1995/96. World sugar consumption 1996/97, adjusted for unrecorded trade, is forecast at 122.9 million tonnes, up nearly 4 per cent from the revised 1995/96 estimate. Record production is expected in countries like Guatemala, Brazil, Thailand and Australia. Significant production increases are likely to be recorded for South Africa, Turkey and Poland. Overall world sugar production 1996/97 is expected to exceed consumption and increase global sugar stocks by 2.1 million tonnes. Russia, China and the USA are expected to be the leading sugar importers in 1996/97, with Cuba and Ukraine continuing as largest supplier to Russia, USDA added. The jump in consumption is mainly due to increased offtake in Asia with India, China, Indonesia and the Philippines being the most dynamic markets.

Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foodstuffs (GEZA) has bought 13,000 tonnes of raw sugar at $292.75 a tonne, a GEZA official recently said. The quantity will be delivered between December 20, 1996 and January 20, 1997. It was added that the sugar was bought from French company Lorico. GEZA had canceled a bid for 13,000 tonnes of white sugar which was part of the same tender, issued on November 5 as price offers did not meet GEZA's conditions.
